rule.description: A COM interface wrapper exposes a method of a COM capability family (identity/lifetime, late binding by name, element enumeration, connection advising, type/runtime metadata) that the wrapper's own native COM vtable contract does not include, and/or a declared Go interface spans several unrelated COM capability families so that every wrapper is forced to carry families its own contract does not own.

checks.description: Detect COM wrapper methods that belong to a capability family the wrapper's own native COM vtable contract does not include; every added umbrella-fulfilment body and capability override is a violation because the underlying COM interface cannot honor the declaration.
checks.detected_relation: wrapper method -> capability family absent from the wrapper's native vtable slots
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Implementors of the broad handle are forced to declare capabilities they do not own, so consumers depend on method promises that fail at runtime instead of being prevented at compile time.

checks.description: Detect a declared Go interface spanning several unrelated COM capability families such that every wrapper in the family is forced to carry capability methods its own contract does not own, through embedding of the base handle.
checks.detected_relation: umbrella interface -> unowned capability methods forced onto each wrapper family member
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: One all-purpose interface exceeds every implementor's dependency boundary: identity-only wrappers get late-binding, enumeration and advising obligations purely to satisfy the shared abstraction.

excluded.reason: Return concrete root handles and take no handle parameter; no capability obligation is represented.
Deprecated fluent API declared on concrete struct types with frozen surface; it does not depend on a generic handle abstraction.
An emulated COM server-side vtable callback shim, not a wrapper type and not a consumer of the umbrella.
Data payload helpers without vtable-backed interface identity; no owned capability families.
These wrappers declare only methods their own vtable slots own (type metadata, advising); they match the umbrella relation as forced implementors but are themselves unchanged by the diff.
